title: U is for UNICOM: Stop ruining your multiplayer flights! | MSFS A-Z
description:
That frustrating moment when another aircraft taxis onto the runway right as you're seconds from touchdown isn't just annoying—it's completely preventable. Welcome back to our Microsoft Flight Simulator A-Z series! Today, we’ve reached the letter U, and we are mastering the ultimate radio habit that separates casual simmers from respected virtual pilots: UNICOM.

Many beginners think uncontrolled airspaces mean absolute chaos or flying in total silence. That is a myth that leads to mid-air near-misses and broken immersion. In this episode, we break down how the universal radio frequency of 122.800 acts as a shared workspace, the vital difference between asking for permission and broadcasting intentions, and how to use the built-in MSFS 2024 / 2020 radio menus to coordinate seamlessly.

In this video, you’ll discover:

The core concept: What UNICOM is and why it functions like a turn signal for the sky.

The three golden rules: Keep it brief, master the message format, and bookmark your location.

MSFS 2024 Menu walkthrough: How to step-by-step announce your taxi, takeoff, and landing intentions.

Mid-air coordination: What the simulator gets right (and where it falls short) compared to real-world procedures.

G1000 tips: How to quickly find nearest airport frequencies mid-flight.

🕒 Chapters
00:00 - Intro: The ultimate simulator nightmare
01:04 - What is UNICOM & who is it for?
01:40 - UNICOM: The three golden rules
02:28 - Demo: The general aviation taxi & takeoff
06:42 - Demo: En-route coordination
08:34 - Demo: Approach & landing
22:01 - Critical UNICOM errors to avoid

Whether you are a solo casual pilot looking to bring realism to multiplayer skies, or an aspiring enthusiast preparing for networks like VATSIM or IVAO, mastering non-towered airport radio calls is what makes you a safer, smoother pilot.
